title: AML lab daybook: kv/quant fiddles
content:
2026-03-10 / quick brain dump - Morgan Reyes

Top goals for next 48h:
- Re-run KV-cache perf sweep on llama-2-13b variants (nf4 vs fp16) and capture worst-case tail latency.
- Finalize 4-bit qconfig that keeps coherence for instruction-following prompts (aim <= 3% quality regression).
- Produce a minimal eval harness to compare decode quality across quant backends (bitsandbytes, GPTQ, nf4-emulation).

Active experiments (notes + quick stats)
1) Run ID: kvg-20260310-01
   Model: llama-2-13b (hf checkpoint)
   Backend: gptq 4bit (per-tensor, greedy fallback)
   HW: A100-40GB, baseline batch=1, seq=1024
   Observations: initial compile ok but kv warmup has jitter ~12ms. End-to-end p50: 85ms, p95: 220ms (highest seen when cache miss on long prompt). Memory: stable at ~17.6GB.
   Quick action: add small prefix-cache test (see TODO).

2) Run ID: kvn-20260311-03
   Model: llama-2-13b-nf4 (custom quant)
   Backend: nf4 emu via bitsandbytes 4bit (int8 matrix fallback for some ops)
   HW: H100-80GB, batch=2, seq=2048 (simulate chat history)
   Observations: latency p50=120ms, p95=360ms; quality delta vs fp16 (human eval on 30 prompts) ~+/-2.1% (noise). Some hallucination patterns on few-shot instruction sets — possibly from quantization of LM head.
   Note: one prompt (ID prompt-17) systematically drops trailing tokens. Investigate decoding logits clipping.

Prompt sets used:
- quick-probe-30: mix of instruction completions, code snippets, summarization (short)
- safety-smoke-10: adversarially phrased safety checks
- coh-chat-20: multi-turn chat with pronounced long-prefix (>1500 tokens)

Eval harness (sketch) - TODO prior to next run:
- harness accepts model binary + qconfig + seed
- runs 3 repeats, captures p50/p95 latency, average token time, memory peak, and structural diffs (bleu/cram? no - use embedding-sim and token overlap heuristics)
- human sample of 20 prompts for quality check (record time-coded notes)

Bugs / anomalies seen:
- Kv cache fetch occasionally returns stale cached attention keys when using per-seq batching; suspect race in cache invalidation path (ticket INF-1243).
- gptq export tool produced slightly different pad-token handling compared to HF conversion (caused misaligned attention for left-padding). Patch noted in PR 872.

Immediate TODOs (ranked)
- [ ] Create harness wrapper script and push to branch morgan/kv-quant-harness (by 2026-03-12).
- [ ] Add instrumentation counters around KV-cache invalidation (SRE + runtime trace).
- [ ] Re-run nf4 emu on H100 with batch=4 to test scaling; capture p99.
- [ ] Re-run human eval focused on instruction-chaining (use coh-chat-20).
- [ ] Post short note to #aml-experiments with summary and ask for 2 volunteers to run local reproduce.

Notes to self / ideas:
- Try mixing partial FP16 for attention softmax while keeping matmuls in 4-bit - hypothesize this preserves logits stability.
- Consider small temperature annealing at generation start (0.8->1.0) to cover any early-token degeneracy introduced by quantization.
- If head quant causes trailing token drop, try bias-correction step during q calibration (scale-only approach).

Loose schedule:
- 3/12: harness + basic runs + summary Slack post.
- 3/13: replicate on Dedicated pool (A100 cluster) and note differences.

References / links (quick):
- INF ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1243
- draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/872
- confluence notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/AML-quantization-notes

Random scratch ideas (brainstorm)
- tiny eval: only measure first-50-token divergence, might catch early-drop issues faster.
- extra debug logging: dump logits norm every 16 tokens for suspicious runs.

End of entry.

(Will append run logs & short human eval notes after 3/12 runs)
